subject: Renewal + capacity top-up for Solstice Health — headroom/price-safeguard options
messages:
From: Anna Morales <anna@solsticehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity top-up request

Olga —

Hope you’re well. We’re kicking off our FY28 budgeting and usage projections and wanted to start the renewal conversation early. Over the past 9 months our token consumption on the Redwood hosted API has grown ~2.9x and forecasting suggests we’ll need about 1.4x our current committed capacity for the next 12 months.

Key asks from my side:
- A renewal that covers the upcoming 12 months with predictable unit pricing (our procurement team needs price stability).
- Options for a one-time headroom/top-up credit to cover burst growth while we finalize our internal forecasting.
- Any flexibility on discounting tied to an increased commit or multi-quarter term is helpful.

Can you share a couple of options (term/commit/discount/headroom credit) and any doc we can share with procurement? I’ll loop in procurement once we have a number to evaluate.

Thanks —
Anna Morales
Director, Platform Integrations
Solstice Health

---
Attachment: none

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Anna Morales <anna@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity top-up request

Anna — thank you for the heads-up and the projection. Appreciate you starting early. Below are two pragmatic paths we can take; I’ve attached a short worksheet (proposal_v3.xlsx) with line item math so procurement can see both the unit economics and the one-time credit impact.

Option 1 — 12-month price hold (quicker sign):
- Commit: 1.25x current committed units
- List unit price: $0.0032/token
- Applied discount: 10% off list on committed units
- One-time headroom credit: $20,000 applied as pre-paid usage credit
- Price hold duration: 12 months from execution

Option 2 — 24-month price hold (deeper savings):
- Commit: 1.5x current committed units
- List unit price: $0.0032/token
- Applied discount: 18% off list on committed units
- One-time headroom credit: $40,000 applied as pre-paid usage credit
- Price hold duration: 24 months from execution

A practical middle ground we sometimes use: 9-month price hold plus a larger one-time headroom credit. If procurement needs a shorter price guarantee but wants meaningful short-term protection, that is viable too.

Notes/assumptions:
- Headroom credits are one-time pre-paid usage credits applied before committed consumption and expire six months after execution unless consumed.
- If usage materially exceeds the committed bucket for sustained periods we’ll discuss converting overage into committed increases at the agreed committed unit price.

If you’d like I can draft an amendment reflecting Option 1 and the middle-ground 9-month variant so procurement has a clean doc to review. Loop in procurement and I’ll bring Marissa into the thread for the onboarding/support details.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

From: Anna Morales <anna@solsticehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@solsticehealth.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity top-up request

Thanks, Olga — this is helpful. Procurement’s main constraints: they need a clearly stated price-hold clause, and they prefer a one-time credit of at least $50k if we go with a shorter term (9–12 months) because that helps our internal capex smoothing.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) Offer a $50k headroom/top-up credit on a 9-month price hold?
2) If not, what’s the closest structure to get us to that budget outcome (e.g., higher commit + smaller credit)?

I’ve added procurement on this thread (procurement@solsticehealth.com) so they can chime in on timing and PO requirements.

—Anna

Subject: Fwd: Solstice renewal — approval request for $50k headroom credit (deal RDW-2027-3498)

Marissa/Marcus — looping you both for quick approvals and to document the ask. Solstice wants a $50k one-time headroom/top-up credit in exchange for a relatively short 9-month price-hold window. Their preference is to avoid a 24-month lock.

Suggested commercial we can present to procurement if approved:
- Commit: 1.35x current committed units (midpoint)
- Unit price: $0.0032/token with 15% discount on committed units
- One-time headroom credit: $50,000 applied as pre-paid usage credit, expires 6 months after execution
- Price hold: 9 months from execution
- Required: signed amendment + PO by June 1st (to meet billing & entitlement cycles)

Impact note: This is slightly more aggressive on credit than our standard guide — roughly a $50k hit versus baseline. I attached the proposal_v3 worksheet and a quick margin calc. If we approve, I’ll prepare the amendment and route via DocuSign.

Could you reply with approval or suggested changes? Procurement is waiting on a concrete answer.

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Solstice renewal — approval request for $50k headroom credit (deal RDW-2027-3498)

Olga — reviewed. Approve the $50k headroom credit on the following guardrails:
1) Lock price for 9 months (no retroactive changes).
2) Commit set to 1.35x current levels; committed units must be invoiced as such.
3) Headroom credit is accounted as a contra-revenue/usage credit and expires 6 months after execution.
4) Amendment must be signed and PO received by June 1st — if not, the credit will be reduced to $30k and we revert to standard 12-month pricing.

Marissa — please prepare the amendment exhibit language and route to legal if required. I’ll prepare a DocuSign envelope and the billing note.
